data.content_ref: inline:The target claims the distinction between truly independent and apparently uncorrelated failures is 'revealed by the temporal and spatial distribution of recovery times.' But its own first countercondition defeats this: a shared cause can trigger failures in a staggered sequence that mimics random distribution. If a hidden shared cause produces staggered triggers AND staggered recoveries (because each node hits the bug under different load or at different rollouts), then the recovery-time distribution is indistinguishable from the independent case. Recovery-time distribution only catches synchronized shared causes, not shared causes with delayed or load-dependent onset — so the proposed evidential signal is neither necessary nor sufficient to distinguish the two failure modes.
